acceptanceCriteria: an ort-ours merge that drops the other side's conflict hunks is reported per file and hunk, not just as an aggregate count
the batch check refuses or marks UNKNOWN until each dropped hunk is covered by a later bound change or an explicit disposition
the merge-resolution-unbound refusal names a recovery that cannot silently lose the other side
regression test with a two-sided conflict proving the dropped side is surfaced
body: Observed 2026-10-18 on claude/sta-ci-1697 (PR beamfall/corvint#1100). A hand-resolved main merge is refused with merge-resolution-unbound, and the known recovery is `git merge -X ours` plus a separately bound fix commit. Merge 8a420f0d2 (-X ours of origin/main 70a21da5d) silently dropped main's side in five files: docs/specs/README.md row, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, docs/decisions/README.md 0543 row, two Makefile .PHONY names (windows-vet, lane-scripts-test; no check catches this), and internal/contextindex/analyzer_schema_test.go audit pins (caught only by TestAnalyzerSchemaInputs). dogfood-batch-check still PASSED (derivation=ort-ours, note conflict-side-dropped merges=19). Only a manual replay as a plain merge found the losses; they were repaired in c3cce7994. Expected: batch-check (or the recovery it names) surfaces each dropped conflict side as an unknown or a refusal, listing the files and hunks, and the recommended recovery does not lose the other side silently (e.g. bind a hand resolution as its own derivation, or require a replay diff of dropped hunks).
title: dogfood-batch-check accepts -X ours merges that silently drop the other side's hunks; the merge-resolution-unbound recovery steers agents into it
